137.t: Terrence Holder and Andy Kirk takes over the band
137.s: Durham was with Holder's band only a few weeks before Holder ran off, apparently with the money, and Andy Kirk was given the band.
137.ch: Kansas City bands and the Blue Devils
137.q: Yeah, and then I went in there, just a little while, may not be over two or three weeks. And Teaholder run off and left the band. Now, some run away with him.

137.t: Between the Battle show and Moten: Kansas City, Oklahoma bands, Blue Devils
137.s: Asked what came next, he lists Gene Coy, Jesse Stone, Terrence Holder and Walter Page's Blue Devils, each only for weeks, before joining Moten.
137.ch: Kansas City bands and the Blue Devils
137.q: I think I went back to Kansas City, yeah, something like that. And then I played with -- I stayed in Kansas City around -- before I joined Benny Morton, I was there in Kansas City a couple of years.

137.t: Joining the Blue Devils through Buster Smith and Booker Pittman
137.s: He knew Buster Smith and Booker Pittman from the Blue Moon Chasers and moved on to the Blue Devils when he got hungry.
137.ch: Kansas City bands and the Blue Devils
137.q: Which was a good band, because they had Booker Pittman, (inaudible) and Buddy Johnson was in that band, Herschel, and when ______ went out, I think Buster Smith came in. And you hear them, you get with that band a little while and then -- let's go to the Blue Devils. You get hungry and you go to…

137.s: Walter Page led the Blue Devils, though Durham thinks someone else may earlier have led.
137.ch: Kansas City bands and the Blue Devils

137.t: Blue Devils personnel and why it broke up
137.s: He lists Lips Page, Walter Page, Buster Smith, Dan Minor, Alvin Burroughs and Jimmy Rushing; the money was light so he left for Moten.
137.ch: Kansas City bands and the Blue Devils
137.q: Let me see, it was Lips Page, Walter Page, Buster Smith, Dan Miner, -- who they never mention, he came from there into Benny Morton's band, trombone player.

66.t: John joins the band; Jimmy Lunceford fills in for him in Memphis
66.s: The Williams combo was doing well at the White Rose when John left to join a band; Lunceford replaced him for six months while she finished dates. She also relates the band's meeting about T. Holder.
66.ch: Memphis, Oklahoma, the Kirk band and Kansas City
66.q: Well, just about 6 months or so because/She I had to leave - wouldn't trust me - I mean wouldn't... because of conditions that existed like that in Tennessee. So what happened, John got this terrific combo going out at the White Rose or something like that. in Memphis. We were just doing real great…

66.t: Andy Kirk takes over from T. Holder
66.s: Within three months the band voted out T. Holder, who had gambled the pay, and made Andy Kirk leader. She travelled with them but did not join as a member until 1931.
66.ch: Memphis, Oklahoma, the Kirk band and Kansas City
66.q: I think it was a matter of about 3 months because I remember going to their first rehearsal and the next 2 or 3 was a meeting when they decided to get rid of Teholder because he had gambled away their salary for that week and he had been doing that all along.

66.t: Arriving in Oklahoma City: sitting in with the band and its gentlemen
66.s: At first she was only John's wife, driving and called in to play 'Froggy Bottom' when the band was stuck. She remembers the musicians as young, well-dressed gentlemen.
66.ch: Memphis, Oklahoma, the Kirk band and Kansas City
66.q: No, I was there as John's wife but he was very shrewd about it. He had his way of working me in. The pianist was very, very great but not as exciting. He was more of a - how shall I say it? - legit pianist, very beautiful chords and very wonderful pianist. So what I did was to go out on trips with…

418.t: Bennie Moten's band splits and Thamon Hayes forms the Rockets
418.s: After the Moten band split, Thamon Hayes took half and formed what became the Kansas City Rockets; Dickenson left for Cincinnati and Clarence Page.
418.q: He capped everybody with that -- that'd do it you know. So the guys who were in London came. And they -- there was -- they had some kind of a thing going on where the guys were fighting each other or something. You know -- disagreeing -- in the Bennie Moten (PHONETIC) band. So they -- they split.…

418.t: Bennie Moten's band splits and Thamon Hayes forms the Rockets
418.s: After the Moten band split, Thamon Hayes took half and formed what became the Kansas City Rockets; Dickenson left for Cincinnati and Clarence Page's band.
418.q: fighting each other or something -- you know, disagreeing -- in the Bennie Moten band. So they...they split. Half of them went one way, and half went the other. The one that went...that wasn't...that didn't stay with Bennie was Thamon Hayes. He took the band, Thamon Hayes. And we stayed together…

418.t: Bennie Moten's band splits and Thamon Hayes forms the Rockets
418.s: After the Moten band split, Thamon Hayes took half and formed the Kansas City Rockets; Dickenson went to Cincinnati to play with Clarence Page.
418.ch: Early bands, Calloway to Basie and Kansas City (third typescript)
418.q: He capped everybody with that -- that'd do it you know. So the guys who were in London came. And they -- there was -- they had some kind of a thing going on where the guys were fighting each other or something. You know -- disagreeing -- in the Bennie Moten (PHONETIC) band.

455.t: T. Holder and the two Twelve Clouds of Joy
455.s: Bandleader T. Holder had run off with the original Twelve Clouds of Joy's money, so Andy Kirk got that band while Holder used the name again in Dallas.
455.ch: The Dallas nightclub and Jesse Stone's band
455.q: In other words, we were auditioning. So all of us passed, and we formed this band. Now the band leader was named T. Holder. Now T. Holder was one of the very sharp, good, beautiful trumpet players that had been with Alphonso Trent over the years, and the reason T. Holder was in Dallas is because T.…

455.t: T. Holder strands the band; Jesse Stone takes over
455.s: T. Holder absconds with the money again in Oklahoma, so the band makes Jesse Stone leader and becomes the Blue Serenaders in St. Joseph.
455.ch: The Dallas nightclub and Jesse Stone's band
455.q: First of all, when he left Kansas City -- see, we were all together in this Jesse Stone band from the North Dallas Club.

455.t: Southern Serenaders become Walter Page's Blue Devils
455.s: Budd clarifies that the Southern Serenaders of 1927 became Walter Page's Blue Devils and later Basie's band.
455.ch: The Dallas nightclub and Jesse Stone's band
455.q: Now that's -- but the Southern Serenaders was back up in here like around '27, when I got stranded in Oklahoma City, and we played the concert for her --

68.t: How T. Holder lost his band to Andy Kirk
68.s: Holder drove to Dallas with the payroll, the band gave his job to Andy Kirk, and Holder started another band.
68.q: Well, T. Holder -- they were playing in Tulsa, Oklahoma and I understand -- I know -- see, he married a girl from my home town, from Denison, Texas, which is -- we call it the same thing. It's just a few miles different. A very beautiful lady and she had a beauty parlor in Dallas, so when they were…

68.t: Recruiting Buster Smith and Joe Keyes for Nat Towles
68.s: Tate gets Buster Smith and Joe Keyes to join Nat Towles' band in Dallas and Smith writes arrangements.
68.q: So they sent him back, see. And then they sent out in Kansas City and they got Ben, you know, to come. So now, all the band is breaking up and they're going back to Bennie Moten except -- well, I wasn't with Bennie Moten. But Basie was the last one to leave. So Nat Tolley is working for this man in…

232.t: Holder's gambling and the band voting Andy Kirk in as leader
232.s: Holder gambles away the band's pay; the owner Faulkenberg tells the men to take over the business, and they vote Andy Kirk to run it.
232.ch: Tulsa bands, Trent, Holder and Kirk
232.q: Another thing, he--maybe it is good and maybe it is bad, but T would play--I got to be pretty close to him, because Andy Kirk went on to the big time-that was T. Holder that made that band.

232.t: Melvin Moore first appears with Don Albert's band
232.s: In Tulsa with Don Albert, young Melvin Moore says he will join Fields' band once he finishes high school in Oklahoma City.
232.ch: Melvin Moore, Hammond and the New York trip
232.q: And so, anyway, then we got to kind of move on, there I was, it looked like I always had those good vocalists, and at that time that was what was setting the band then. Now, T. Holder had Billy Maxted and I would talk to T and I don't know anybody this and

85.t: Becoming musical director of McKinney's Cotton Pickers
85.s: Bill McKinney invited him to Detroit as musical director; Roscoe Simmons fronted the band.
85.q: Well, I guess Bill McKinney had invited me to join the orchestra and wanted to know if I would come to Detroit, which I did. It seems to me that Hilton Jefferson and I were in the orchestra together. Were we? Gee, I don’t know what makes me think that.

371.t: McKinney's Cotton Pickers, Don Redman, and muzak dates
371.s: Jones doesn't know the McKinney family and talks about McKinney's Cotton Pickers and commercial muzak dates.
371.ch: Early bands and the road to New York
371.q: I didn’t know them. There was a James McKinney from Pontiac, a jazz pianist, who later became to be well known in that area. You might not have heard of him. I don’t know the ones you are talking about. There was a band called McKinney's Cotton Pickers. They were in Detroit. Don Redman used to…

406.t: Illness in Chattanooga, then McKinney's Cotton Pickers in Baltimore
406.s: Left behind sick in Chattanooga, he joined McKinney's Cotton Pickers, who fired McKinney and moved to Carlin's Park in Baltimore. With Roy Eldridge in the band he jammed around town every night.
406.ch: Zach White, Cotton Pickers and Cab Calloway
406.q: So I stayed with Zach up until I got sick in Chattanooga, Tennessee and they left me there. Left me in Chattanooga. I stayed in Chattanooga about two, three months, recuperating, then I got a telegram to join McKinney's Cotton Pickers. And I went up to Pennsylvania to play with them. And while I…

17.t: Replacing Leroy Maxey in Cab Calloway's band
17.s: Cole replaces Maxey, who left for Kansas City then illness.
17.ch: Dancers, Newton, Chu Berry and the Cab Calloway band
17.q: I don't know. I think Leroy had been with Cab so long I guess he wanted to go back home to Kansas City, I know that's where I saw him. We played Kansas City.

166.t: Walter Page and Ernie Fields in Oklahoma
166.s: Clarifies where he saw Walter Page.
166.ch: Clarifications and portraits: Lester Young, Byas, Blanton, Ben Webster
166.q: No, I never did hear his band. But I was aware of it. Like, sometimes he would make trips to Tulsa by himself, just to come over to Tulsa, you know, when he was idle. Say, 'Who's that?' Say, 'That's Walter Page of the Blue Devils.'

167.t: Original members and replacing Buddy Blurton
167.s: The original Nephews were Leo Watson, Doug Daniels, Virgil Scoggins and Buddy Blurton, all from St. Louis; Bunn took tiple player Buddy's place and stayed with Bernie about six months.
167.ch: Spirits of Rhythm and the road in the 1930s
167.q: He lived in -- Kansas City? No. Yeah, Kansas City. They're all out of Kansas City.

758.t: Eldridge Brothers Rhythm Kings in Pittsburgh
758.s: After a wire warned him off New York Roy and Joe formed a Pittsburgh band with Kenny Clarke and beat local bands, then left for McKinney's.
758.q: : No, what happened was that... It was a time that I was with Connie's Hot Chocolates on the road. And I got a wire from my buddy telling me, don't come back to New York, they're waiting for me at the station, at the airport, anywhere I'd come in, you know. So I went to Pittsburgh. It was something…

86.t: Alphonso Trent's band breaks up; Jeter-Pillars forms
86.s: He describes Trent's band and its members, and how Jeter and Pillars formed their own band out of its remains.
86.q: No, they were from Texas. They were originally from Texas. Je ter Pillars -- they were from Arkansas. Alphonso Trent, he's from Arkansas, too. But the band got its prominence in Texas because they were the first black band to play on radio from a hotel called the Adolphus Hotel.

473.t: Wesley Helvey's Troubadors, full of Louisville band alumni
473.s: Helvey's band had Jeff Cass, Milt Robinson, John L. Henderson, George Loving and drummer Charles Bloomer, all from the Louisville kid band, and paid better than Horace.
473.ch: Midwest bands: Hardy Brothers, Helvey and Buffalo
473.q: Yeah, he was bigger before, and I think he probably cut it down, and then he wanted to -- because when I got there, another one of the fellows out of the band was playing the trumpet. His name was Jeff Cass, and he had come out of Louisville, out of that band. We had played together, and he was on…
